# opencode-notion-auth [![release](https://github.com/fibbery/opencode-notion-auth/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fibbery/opencode-notion-auth/actions/workflows/release.yml) Notion AI in magpie and OpenCode. Provider id: `notion`. The picture is Notion's own mark, linked from Notion's site rather than bundled here: it says which service the plugin speaks to. The mark stays theirs, and nothing here is affiliated with or endorsed by Notion. The plugin talks to the same API Notion's own AI panel uses, with the `token_v2` cookie a signed-in browser holds. There is no separate Notion API for this and no key to ask for: the cookie is the whole credential. > **Unofficial, and against Notion's terms of service.** Automated access > is very likely not allowed, and the account that carries it is the thing > at risk. Point it at a throwaway workspace, not the one you work in. > Nothing here is affiliated with or endorsed by Notion, and none of their > marks or artwork are included. ## Install ```sh magpie plugin add opencode-notion-auth magpie plugin login notion magpie provider test notion ``` In OpenCode, in `opencode.json`, then `opencode auth login`: ```json { "plugin": ["opencode-notion-auth"] } ``` The plugin runs where magpie and OpenCode run their plugins: Bun. The browser-session sign-in reads its cookie database through `bun:sqlite`, imported only when that method is used — elsewhere the other two ways in still work. ## Sign in Three ways in, all saved as a cookie header in magpie's `plugin-auth.json` (OpenCode's `auth.json`), beside every other sign-in: - **Notion email code** — `getLoginOptions` then `sendTemporaryPassword` asks Notion to email a code; handing the code back through `loginWithEmail` returns the same `token_v2` a browser sign-in would. This is Notion's own passwordless flow. - **This computer's browser session** — reads notion.so cookies out of a Chrome, Chrome Canary or Beta, Chromium, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi or Arc cookie database on macOS, decrypting them with the key macOS keeps in the login keychain. The first read may ask for that key. Firefox and Safari are not read. - **Paste a cookie** — a `token_v2` value, or the whole `document.cookie` string. `token_v2` goes first in what is kept, and the `notion_*` cookies beside it follow. Analytics and Cloudflare's bot cookie are left out: a stale `__cf_bm` earns a refusal more often than it helps. Notion ties AI access to the address the sign-in came from, so a cookie carried to another machine or another network tends to draw intermittent `403 trust-rule-denied` answers. Signing in where it runs is steadier. ## Models The list is the account's own, read with `getAvailableModels` — which needs the workspace id, and answers `400` without it. Names and codes are Notion's, the codes go in `api.id`: | magpie | Notion | |---|---| | `notion/opus-5.5` | `albuquerque-quinn` | | `notion/opus-4.7` | `apricot-sorbet-high` | | `notion/gpt-5.4` | `oval-kumquat-medium` | Magpie shows a provider's first 24 models until some are ticked for it; `magpie provider models notion +` shows the lot. Taking the plugin out and adding it again — or a version that changes the list — makes magpie work the ticks out again, which can leave one model shown: tick them once more, and they keep. ## Reasoning effort Each model says which levels it serves, and the plugin offers them as variants. The level rides in the `config` step of the request as `reasoningEffort`, from either the model's variant (`notion/opus-5.5:high`) or a `reasoning_effort` field. `ultra` is sent as `max`; a level the model does not serve is left out. Notion's thinking arrives as a signature with no text, so no agent shows its reasoning. ## Tool calls Notion AI has no client tool calling: its tools run on Notion's servers and a caller cannot add its own. The plugin asks for a call in the only way left — in words: 1. The client's tools go into the prompt, with names, descriptions and JSON Schema. 2. The model is written to as the planner of a coding agent whose runtime executes the actions, and asked to answer with one action envelope and nothing else: `{"tool":"Read","arguments":{"file_path":"…"}}`. 3. That envelope becomes a real `tool_calls` / `function_call` for the client, and the tool's output returns in the next turn as ``. So a tool-using agent works with this, and it works the way an emulation does: - **One call per turn.** A task that needs three actions takes four turns. - **A tool-using request is answered in one piece.** Until the envelope closes there is no telling prose from a call, so nothing streams. - **A miss is quiet.** When the model answers in prose instead of asking, the client sees an ordinary answer and the loop ends there — the same shape as a model that decided no action was needed. - **No parallel calls, no `tool_choice`, no attachments.** Text tools only. Measured on one account, four short tasks: 9 of 9 turns that needed a call produced one, with 3–13 s a turn. That is not a success rate, only what a few runs looked like; treat the emulation as suited to light work rather than to a main agent loop. ## Notes `getAvailableModels` and `runInferenceTranscript` are internal endpoints of Notion's web app, names and payloads included. They can change without notice, and a release that follows will be needed when they do. The request carries `notion-client-version`, read from the `data-notion-version` attribute of Notion's login page, and `notion_browser_id` when the sign-in knows one, so the traffic looks like the browser's own. ## Licence and provenance MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Written for this plugin; no code was copied from another project. The Notion side of it was researched from these, whose licences are respected and whose authors deserve the credit: - [galiais/notion2api](https://github.com/galiais/notion2api) (MIT): the `runInferenceTranscript` transcript shape, the workspace discovery call and the login sequence. - [Youahui/notion2api](https://github.com/Youahui/notion2api) (Apache-2.0): the tagged tool-call form this plugin still accepts alongside its envelope. - [coldvisixn/cogway](https://github.com/coldvisixn/cogway) (source available, not open source): prior art for writing to the model as a planner rather than as the agent. Its text and code were not taken, and the framing here is written independently. Nothing of anyone else's is redistributed: the picture magpie shows is a link to Notion's own asset, and no vendor artwork is bundled in this package.
